question: Does exposing the rational-point trace homomorphism as exact parity clauses improve the four-free-leaf chained-S3 search on the frozen N53 and N83 targets?
mathematical_source: Kosters and Yeo, Notes on summation polynomials, arXiv:1503.08001v3, Section 4.2, Proposition 4.2; https://arxiv.org/html/1503.08001v3
mathematical_scope: For E: y^2+xy=x^3+1 over F_(2^n), phi(P)=Tr(x(P)) is additive for rational points; phi(-P)=phi(P). In the declared normal basis every basis vector has trace one, so Tr(x) is the XOR of its coordinate bits. Any genuine nonidentity chained-S3 relation obeys parity(x0)+parity(x1)+parity(mid0)=0, parity(x2)+parity(x3)+parity(mid1)=0, and parity(mid0)+parity(mid1)+parity(target_x)=0. These are necessary conditions only; retain independent group replay.
controlled_change: Append exact Tseitin CNF for the three trace-parity equations to each unchanged Q1475 ordered-leaf CNF. Keep the same native solver binary, target inputs, bases, decision policy, and resource caps.
validation_gates: verify normal-basis coordinate parity equals field trace and the trace homomorphism on independently constructed rational points at N53 and N83
verify every appended XOR gate exhaustively and retain all parent CNF clauses byte-for-byte
recover and independently replay the two pinned sorted controls before free-leaf cases
retain all capped, absent, error, and successful case receipts; independently replay any returned four-point relation
selection_scope: The N53 full-coset target was selected for a known-representable control in Q1474 after its pair-table witness was known. It is not an unbiased yield observation. The ordinary targets were frozen before Q1476 and have one query per degree.
claim_limit: Trace parity is a sound necessary condition, not a solution method by itself. Pinned controls do not estimate natural yield. Censored free-leaf cases do not measure successful solve cost. CPU wall intervals without host isolation are exploratory. No complete N131 work exponent or sub-2^61 claim follows from this design.
